=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:822-830 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In resolve_max_rounds_per_item, the digit-only regex `re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+", value, flags=re.ASCII)` has no length limit, so on Python 3.11+ a UNBLOCK_MAX_ROUNDS_PER_ITEM value longer than 4300 digits passes the regex and `number = int(value)` (line 829) then raises ValueError.
  WHY: The ValueError leaves decide() uncaught (main() at lines 1360-1368 catches only UsageError and InputError), so scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2177 logs outcome=skip reason=decide_failed for every item, which breaks the docstring promise "A bad value never fails `decide`"; all four reviewers rated it NIT, mapped here to low.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:3500 (mirror at .github/workflows/clarify.yml:2342) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In `((((.check_run_url // "") | capture("/check-runs/(?<id>[1-9][0-9]*)$") | .id) // .id) | tostring)`, `capture` raises on a non-match and `//` does not catch errors, so the `// .id` fallback never runs.
  WHY: The jq program aborts, `2>/dev/null || true` swallows the error, FP_JOB_ID is empty, the guard at plan.yml:3501/3502 skips the annotations fetch, and no AI_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_V1 marker is emitted, so the P3b breaker cannot trip; z-ai_glm-5_3-flash says the bug only happens on jq 1.6 and that the fallback is reachable on 1.7+; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rejected this finding, saying a non-matching `capture` gives an empty stream (not checked with jq) and that the line is outside this PR's diff; all flaggers rated it NIT, mapped here to low.
- scripts/ai_labels.py:1142-1143, 1229-1257 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The 180-second drain deadline is checked only before each item, so if it expires during the final item the code still does the final listing and can return success, which lets the caller delete the label after the deadline.
  WHY: Each API request can take up to 120 seconds (timeout at line 268), so slow sequential requests can overrun the 180-second budget and approach the workflow's 5-minute timeout without deferring, and the run can be killed before it logs a completed drain; source rated it NIT.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:31 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The header comment still says "2 rounds per item", but the cap is now `UNBLOCK_MAX_ROUNDS_PER_ITEM` (default 3, clamped 1-5) per scripts/unblock_ledger.py:206.
  WHY: The comment has no runtime effect but now misstates the enforced cap; scripts/unblock_judge.sh is outside the #8813 files_touched grant; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 raised the same point as a hardening suggestion rather than a finding; source rated it NIT.
- tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py, tests/test_orchestrate_lib.py, tests/test_session_start_extract_repo_slug.py, tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py:pre-push test gate | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The pre-push gate lists these four test files under "Failures caused by this change", but neither the PR diff nor the last-run diff touches the files they audit, so the failures cannot be mapped to any code site.
  WHY: The gate blocks the pipeline until these pass, so the editor must re-run them on the merged tree and either fix the regression or correct the attribution; tests/test_unblock_judge.py is also reported "Unverified" (baseline_timeout, 6 changed pre-existing assertions); source rated it MAJOR, mapped here to high; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 said these failures are not mapped to this diff and should be re-run rather than edited for.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:822-830 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: In resolve_max_rounds_per_item, the digit-only regex has no length limit, so a digit string longer than 4300 characters makes `number = int(value)` raise ValueError on Python 3.11+, and main() at lines 1360-1368 catches only UsageError and InputError.
  WHY: scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2177 treats the non-zero exit as decide_failed, so every judge run for every item skips, which contradicts the docstring "A bad value never fails `decide`, so the item is still judged"; suggested fix: `number = int(value) if len(value) <= 3 else MAX_ROUNDS_PER_ITEM_CEILING + 1`.

  PROBLEM: `resolve_max_rounds_per_item` lacks a length check on the input string before calling `int()`.
  WHY: A very long string can cause a ValueError (Python's integer string conversion limit), so `decide` fails and the item is skipped instead of falling back to the configured cap.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:829 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: In resolve_max_rounds_per_item, `re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+", value, flags=re.ASCII)` has no length cap, and on Python 3.11+ int() raises ValueError for digit strings longer than sys.get_int_max_str_digits() (default 4300).
  WHY: A 5000+ digit UNBLOCK_MAX_ROUNDS_PER_ITEM value makes the exception propagate out of decide(), so the judge logs outcome=skip reason=decide_failed, which contradicts the docstring ("A bad value never fails `decide`").

  WHY: jq aborts, `2>/dev/null || true` leaves FP_JOB_ID empty, the annotations fetch is skipped, and no AI_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_V1 marker is appended, so the P3b breaker cannot trip for that run.
